classification.difficultyReason: Form parameter-dependent discriminants and interpret their negative intervals, including a non-negative perfect square with no solution.

content.prompt:
In each case, find the discriminant $\Delta$ and solve $\Delta<0$ to find any values of $\lambda$ for which the parabola has no $x$-intercepts.

(Hint: Either a graph of $\Delta$ versus $\lambda$ or a table of test points may help.)

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=\lambda^2-4(1)(1)\\\Delta&=\lambda^2-4\\\lambda^2-4&<0\\(\lambda-2)(\lambda+2)&<0\end{align*}$$
The graph of $\Delta=\lambda^2-4$ opens upwards and crosses the $\lambda$-axis at $-2$ and $2$. It is below the axis between these values.

Hence $-2<\lambda<2$.

$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=6^2-4\lambda(\lambda)\\\Delta&=36-4\lambda^2\\\Delta&=4(9-\lambda^2)\\4(9-\lambda^2)&<0\end{align*}$$
The graph of $\Delta=4(9-\lambda^2)$ opens downwards and crosses the $\lambda$-axis at $-3$ and $3$. It is below the axis outside these values.

Hence $\lambda<-3$ or $\lambda>3$.

$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(1-\lambda)^2-4(1)(-\lambda)\\\Delta&=1-2\lambda+\lambda^2+4\lambda\\\Delta&=\lambda^2+2\lambda+1\\\Delta&=(\lambda+1)^2\end{align*}$$
A square is never negative, so there are no values of $\lambda$ for which $\Delta<0$. Thus the parabola always has at least one $x$-intercept.

$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(-2\lambda)^2-4\lambda[-(\lambda-2)]\\\Delta&=4\lambda^2+4\lambda(\lambda-2)\\\Delta&=8\lambda^2-8\lambda\\\Delta&=8\lambda(\lambda-1)\\8\lambda(\lambda-1)&<0\end{align*}$$
The graph of $\Delta=8\lambda(\lambda-1)$ opens upwards and crosses the $\lambda$-axis at $0$ and $1$. It is below the axis between these values.

Hence $0<\lambda<1$.
